quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose footwear with soles that:

options.text: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
Are made of soft, flimsy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a group of riders small is:

options.text: A small group is less easily separated in traffic than a larger group.
A small group can disregard traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up to the group.
It will be difficult to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is less easily separated in traffic than a larger group.
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to get separated by traffic or stop lights, and don't require slower riders to rush to catch up.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts the wearer's vision to the sides.
Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
Makes it more difficult for the wearer to control their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: A helmet improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: Let the tailgater get in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may only increase danger by making them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: If you wait an hour per alcoholic drink before you ride your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by causing them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces provide poor tire traction. These include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way you would without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are only for you, the driver.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be equipped and adjusted to safely carry a passenger. Your motorcycle needs a separate seat large enough for two people and footrests for the passenger. You may also need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, this means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts affecting you.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts affecting you.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly without needing digestion. It reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour, which is relatively slow.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear brightly-colored clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothing should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but not your legs.
Cover your legs completely, but not your arms.
Be whatever makes you comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs to protect yourself while riding.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored and reflective clothing at all times. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so bright clothing is important even during daylight.

questions.question: When checking tires before riding, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and signs of wear.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay there to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave to get the other driver's attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to move out of it.

questions.question: Which of the following does not need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle's tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Even small mechanical problems can be very dangerous while riding.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen only in areas where it is safe and legal to pass.

questions.question: While sitting on your motorcycle before riding, check everything except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check that your brakes, clutch, throttle, turn signals, lights, horn, and mirrors all work properly.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals tell other drivers your next move. When your left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters show traffic rules, like speed limits. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
